typed: I draw my arming sword and push through the crowd toward the woman in the embroidered collar, ready to confront her.
note: Nice opening scene. The face that turned away is a good hook.
Odds screen is clear. "Go big" is unexplained though, I don't know what it changes. Also "you lose your footing" appears for both fail and badly, which reads a bit repetitive.
Odds screen is clear. Going big raised the stakes without changing odds, which is a clean trade-off. Failure jumps to "serious/grave" but never says concretely what that costs.

typed: I scramble up and lunge at the woman in the collar bare-handed, grabbing her arm before she can speak.
note: The fumble scene was vivid. The result line doesn't say whether I'm actually hurt (health?), only "grave", which is vague.
Odds screen is clear. Mildly odd that the "Very well" chance went from 15% to 25% here; otherwise fine.
Fine overall. Going big again shows the same odds with higher stakes, which is clear. Pressing Enter just repeated the screen, which is slightly redundant but understandable.
Near-miss screen is clear, though "serious" cost isn't spelled out in plain terms, and the prompt was left blank so I had to guess what Enter does.

typed: I keep hold of her sleeve and lean in. "What are you saying? Tell me, quickly, before the watch gets here."
note: Fine. Nice tension. One oddity: the sword is "out of reach" but still fine. The result line said "restrained by you" in an awkward fragment.

typed: I keep hold of her with one hand and shout at Eliard across the gap: "Eliard! What is at the gate? Answer plainly, now, before the watch takes her!"
note: The scene is tense and works well. One small oddity: earlier text said the woman "stops struggling", but she hadn't been struggling before. Otherwise fine.

typed: I haul her behind the bar, grab my sword from under the brackets on the way, and tell Eliard: "Done. Now who is the Choir of the Silence, and how many are out there?"
note: Good tension. Slightly unclear whether anything is actually "at the gate" versus the woman herself, and no odds screen appeared for the last two free-form lines, which was fine.

typed: I draw my sword on Eliard and say: "Name and count, now. And if you give the watch my face, I'll give them yours."
note: Eliard's choice is a bit odd since he already said five or six and a name (Choir of the Silence), so the "name and count" offer was already delivered. Otherwise fine.
Offer screen is clear. Slight oddity: the text said I'd get a name and a count, but the offer only covers the leader's name.
Fine. The odds screen is clear, and the go-big stakes bump is easy to follow.

typed: I lunge at Eliard with my sword and try to cut him down before the watch gets over the counter.
note: Good tension. The failed roll was clear, and the back door is a nice hint at an escape route. Nothing confusing.

typed: /fix The game says I'm "pinned" and must break free, but nobody has grabbed me. I'm behind the bar with my sword drawn, and the woman only holds my sleeve. My lunge at Eliard shouldn't be blocked as a grapple.
note: The redirect says I'm pinned, but nothing in the story pinned me. It reads as a wrong state, and it blocked my attack. The last failure text also said my legs stayed planted, which doesn't fit a lunge.
